entries.proposition: The brain data come from nude mice carrying human lung-cancer xenografts; the host brains are not WWOX-deficient.
entries.snippet: Nude mice received subcutaneous injections of these cells twice on both sides of the flanks

entries.proposition: The figure legend reads as one mouse per group.
entries.snippet: Spleen enlargement occurred in all mice except in the mouse harboring WWOX-expressing NCI-H1299

entries.proposition: A housekeeping protein is also reported as aggregated, which weakens the specificity of the aggregation readout.
entries.snippet: Housekeeping protein α-tubulin was also aggregated.

entries.proposition: The authors state the cause of brain aggregation is unknown.
entries.snippet: For unknown reasons, the growing tumors induce protein aggregation in the mouse brain and lung.

entries.proposition: The cytokine mechanism is a belief, not a measurement.
entries.snippet: We believe that cytokines released by growing cancer cells induce protein aggregation.

entries.proposition: How the flank tumours affect the brain is stated as unknown.
entries.snippet: How the tumor cells in the flanks control neurodegeneration in the brain is unknown and remains to be established.

entries.proposition: Yeast two-hybrid: the SDR domain did not bind TIAF1.
entries.snippet: Also, the SDR domain of WWOX did not bind TIAF1.
entries.anchor: Results, TIAF1 binds the first N-terminal WW domain of WWOX

entries.proposition: The FRET section concludes that WWOX joins via the SDR domain, contradicting the yeast two-hybrid result in the same paper.
entries.snippet: WWOX joins the complex via its C-terminal SDR domain to stabilize the complex triad
entries.anchor: Results, Activated p53 binds TIAF1, final sentence

entries.proposition: Statistics are Student’s t-tests in Excel.
entries.snippet: Data were analyzed by Student’s t test among controls and tested groups using Microsoft excel.
